Why go: Samui's own rum, made from island cane

Koh Samui has one working rum distillery, in the quiet south near Ban Thale. It distils fresh sugar-cane juice in the French agricole style rather than from molasses, and flavours some rums with island fruit. A visit is a good rainy-day plan, a change from beaches and temples, and an easy add-on to a day in the south.

What you'll do

The morning tour is short and focused: a welcome drink, a walk through the cane area, the copper still and the ageing room, then a guided tasting. The afternoon workshop is a slower, more social session hosted by the manager, with a cocktail on arrival, a deeper look at fermentation and ageing, and snack platters with the tasting. Both are private for your group.

Who it suits

  • Groups of 4 or more friends, couples travelling with friends, and anyone interested in food and drink.
  • Visitors staying in Lamai, Hua Thanon or the south coast, for whom it is close.

Who should choose something else

  • Couples on their own may find the 4-guest minimum expensive; ask us first.
  • Families with young children will get more from the Thai cooking class.

Good to know

  • Drinking and driving: don't ride a scooter back after the tasting. Thai roads are dangerous enough sober; book the van or a taxi.
  • Season: visit between January and May to see cane crushing and distilling.
  • Nearby: the south coast fishing villages and Thong Krut are 15 minutes away for a seafood lunch.

Before you book

Tell us your group size and whether you want the morning tour or the afternoon workshop; both run on request, so we confirm the session with the distillery before you pay. If you are staying in the north of the island, the drive is the longest part of the trip: pair it with lunch in the south rather than making a special journey just for the tasting.
